case_title: ACL Inverted Wildcard Mask Blocking Web Server

original_ai_diagnosis.root_cause: The ACL rule 10 is missing TCP established flag.
original_ai_diagnosis.suggested_fix:
R1(config)# ip access-list extended 101
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 permit tcp 172.16.10.0 255.255.255.0 host 10.1.1.100 eq www established

human_correction.root_cause: The issue is an inverted wildcard mask (255.255.255.0 was used instead of Cisco wildcard 0.0.0.255), not a missing established flag.
human_correction.corrected_fix:
R1(config)# ip access-list extended 101
R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 10
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 permit tcp 172.16.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.1.1.100 eq www
R1(config-ext-nacl)# end
human_correction.reviewer_notes: The AI hallucinated that the TCP rule required an 'established' keyword, failing to recognize that standard subnet masks in Cisco ACLs act as inverted wildcards and prevent client connection initiation.

lesson_learned: LLMs often confuse standard subnet masks with Cisco ACL wildcard inverse masks. Deterministic regex rule checking is critical to flag '255.255.255.0' inside ACL lines.
guardrail_implemented: Added Deterministic Rule RULE-ACL-001 that intercepts 255.255.255.x strings within access-list statements.

case_title: Interface Administratively Down on Core Trunk

original_ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Spanning-tree root bridge re-election failure or missing OSPF routing statement on Building B distribution switch.
original_ai_diagnosis.suggested_fix:
DS1(config)# router ospf 1
DS1(config-router)# network 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 0

human_correction.root_cause: Interface GigabitEthernet0/24 is 'administratively down'. Physical/Layer 1 shutdown must be resolved before any routing protocol can establish.
human_correction.corrected_fix:
DS1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/24
DS1(config-if)# no shutdown
DS1(config-if)# end
human_correction.reviewer_notes: AI proposed a complex OSPF reconfiguration without checking interface state. The interface was simply administratively disabled.

lesson_learned: AI tends to overcomplicate diagnoses by jumping straight to Layer 3 routing rather than checking basic Layer 1/2 interface status.
guardrail_implemented: Enforced Layer 1 interface status checks to run first in the diagnostic pipeline.

case_title: NAT PAT Failure - Missing Overload Keyword

original_ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Missing overload keyword on NAT statement.
original_ai_diagnosis.suggested_fix: R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload

human_correction.root_cause: Missing overload keyword, PLUS stale static 1-to-1 translations remain in the NAT table until cleared.
human_correction.corrected_fix:
R1(config)# no ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1
R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
R1(config)# end
R1# clear ip nat translation *
human_correction.reviewer_notes: Without negating the old command ('no ip nat inside...') and executing 'clear ip nat translation *', Cisco IOS will reject modifying the NAT rule while active translations exist.

lesson_learned: Cisco IOS requires explicit session clearing when switching from dynamic 1-to-1 NAT to PAT/overload.
guardrail_implemented: Added automatic rollback and translation clearing commands to NAT remediation templates.

case_title: DHCP Pool Exhaustion & Subnet Allocation Error
error_category: Disruptive Fix Timing & Unnecessary Device Reload

original_ai_diagnosis.suggested_fix:
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool POOL_FINANCE
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0
R1# reload

human_correction.root_cause: Subnet mask /28 in DHCP pool was too small. Reloading the router causes production outage for all departments.
human_correction.corrected_fix:
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool POOL_FINANCE
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0
R1(config-dhcp)# end
R1# clear ip dhcp binding *
human_correction.reviewer_notes: AI recommended a full router 'reload'. Network engineers should never reboot production routers when clearing the DHCP binding table is sufficient.

lesson_learned: AI models often suggest drastic measures (like reboots) for software table state issues. Human review prevents unnecessary downtime.
guardrail_implemented: Added risk guardrail flagging 'reload' commands as dangerous.

case_title: Inter-VLAN Routing Failure - Subinterface Tag Mismatch

original_ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Subinterface G0/0/0.20 has wrong dot1Q tag 25.
original_ai_diagnosis.suggested_fix:
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 20

human_correction.root_cause: Subinterface tag mismatch. In Cisco IOS, modifying encapsulation on an existing subinterface removes the IP address.
human_correction.corrected_fix:
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 20
R1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# write memory
human_correction.reviewer_notes: Changing encapsulation dot1Q on Cisco IOS automatically wipes out the configured IP address on that subinterface. The IP address must be re-applied in the same config session.

lesson_learned: Cisco IOS subinterfaces drop their IP configuration when the dot1Q encapsulation tag is altered. Junior engineers and AI frequently miss this side-effect.
guardrail_implemented: Enforced rule that subinterface encapsulation modifications must always be paired with the corresponding 'ip address' command.
